title: onprem/airgap: include additional helm charts + vendored deps for rke2 Ubuntu 22.04 offline bundle
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Several customers running the on-prem/private installer on RKE2 + Ubuntu 22.04 reported airgapped install failures due to missing Helm charts (metrics-server, kube-proxy images hooks) and mismatches in vendored dependencies. This PR updates the offline bundle to include the missing Helm charts, vendors updated chart tarballs and OCI images relevant to RKE2 on Ubuntu 22.04, and refreshes the TUF metadata and apt mirror manifests. Summary of changes: added additional helm chart tarballs (metrics-server, rke2-canal, prometheus-node-exporter) to the offline bundle; vendored updated image layers for rke2 v1.24.14-rke2r1; updated apt mirror snapshot for ubuntu-22.04 (curl/gnupg/libseccomp fixes); refreshed TUF signing metadata and added checksums for new artifacts; added installer hooks to handle systemd kubelet cgroup detection on Ubuntu 22.04; extended rollback tooling to snapshot and restore apt mirror and helm-chart manifests for safe upgrades. Checklist: - [x] Vendor new helm charts and image layer blobs into offline bundle - [x] Update TUF metadata and sign with airgap keyring - [x] Add installer preflight for apt mirror and sysctl/cgroup settings on Ubuntu 22.04 - [x] Add e2e airgap integration test (CI) and manual vSphere validation notes - [x] Update docs and release notes snippet. Testing performed: ran integration/airgap CI pipeline against a local registry mirror (see ci/integration-airgap job below). Performed manual install on Ubuntu 22.04 VMs (vSphere) using the generated offline bundle; exercised upgrade path from previous bundle and validated rollback using the new snapshot tool. Verified TUF verification during install, apt mirror resolution from offline bundle, and systemd kubelet cgroup detection. Rollout notes: This change is non-breaking for existing installs but changes the offline artifact set. Customers performing a bundle replacement should follow the upgrade guide (copy new bundle, run installer with --preview to validate apt and chart manifests, then execute upgrade). The rollback tool included here can restore the previous apt snapshot and helm manifests if the upgrade fails. Related: references ENG-1428 (airgap reliability triage) and SUP-5023 (customer report).
